scenes.say: Ever wondered how large language models actually produce text—and what controls their creativity and recall?

scenes.label: Tokens
scenes.sub: LLMs split text into tokens—words or subwords.
scenes.say: First, LLMs break everything you type into tokens, which are just words or subwords. That’s how they handle language.
Two big factors: context window—the maximum tokens the model can recall at once—and temperature, which tweaks how random or creative the output is.
Set temperature low for focused, predictable answers. Raise it for more creative and varied responses.

scenes.question: Can LLMs recall all previous text?
scenes.right: No, they only see up to their context window limit.
scenes.say: Don’t get caught thinking LLMs remember everything—they only see up to their context window limit.
